title: Shift Sweet Chilli Pork Stir-Fry
method: The listed 75g dry egg noodles is an uncooked weight. Cut the 90g broccoli into small florets. Bring a saucepan of water to the boil, cook the broccoli for 3–4 minutes until just tender, then lift it onto a plate with a slotted spoon. Cook the noodles in the same boiling water for the time on their packet until tender, then drain well. Time this to finish shortly before the pan ingredients are ready.

Deseed and thinly slice the 90g mixed peppers. Cut the 170g lean pork loin into thin strips about 1cm thick on a separate board. Wash hands, the board and knife after handling the raw meat; do not rinse it.

Heat half the listed olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add the lean pork loin in one layer and cook for 7–10 minutes, turning regularly. Lower the heat if the outside browns too quickly. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must reach 70°C for 2 minutes. Keep cooking if it has not reached that endpoint; the suggested time is a guide. Transfer to a clean plate; keep the pan for the vegetables. Never reuse the plate or utensils that held the raw food without washing them.

Add the remaining half of the listed olive oil to the same pan. Add 90g mixed peppers and cook for 4–6 minutes, stirring often, until softened with some bite. Keep the heat moderate so the small measured amount of oil does not smoke.
Add the drained noodles and broccoli to the pan. Toss gently for 1–2 minutes to combine without crushing the florets.

Turn the heat to low and fold in the 40g sweet chilli sauce. Stir for 1–2 minutes until hot, following any longer heating instruction on the sauce label. This measured sauce coats the food; do not boil it dry or add an unlisted jar of sauce.

Return the cooked lean pork loin and its juices to the pan and stir through. Heat gently until the whole pan is steaming hot, stirring to distribute the heat. Divide the noodles, vegetables and lean pork loin between serving bowls. Serve immediately.

title: Shift Club Turkey Hot Toastie

Preheat the sandwich toaster according to its instructions. Use the measured wholemeal bread as two slices and brush all the measured olive oil over the two outer faces.

title: Shift Club Turkey Loaded Jacket Potato
method: Scrub the baking potato and pierce it several times with a fork. For an oven, heat to 200°C (180°C fan), put the potato on a tray and bake for about 60–75 minutes. For an 800W microwave, put it on a microwave-safe plate and cook for 8 minutes, turning halfway; continue in 1-minute bursts as needed. In either case, check the centre is completely soft when pierced and allow it to stand for 2 minutes; size and appliance affect the time.
Wash and dry the mixed salad and spring onion. Trim and slice the spring onion very finely, then mix it with the salad to serve alongside the potato.
Use chilled, already-cooked turkey breast; slice it thinly or shred it into small pieces. Keep it refrigerated until assembly.
Stir together all the measured light mayonnaise, wholegrain mustard and olive oil in a small bowl to make the dressing. Keep it refrigerated until assembly.

Split the cooked potato and fluff the centre with a fork. Add the prepared ready-to-eat filling and the prepared dressing; the filling is served chilled on the hot potato. Serve the full mixed salad and finely sliced spring onion alongside, and eat immediately.

For a packed lunch, cool the cooked potato promptly before covering and refrigerating it; pack the chilled filling, dressing and salad separately. Eat within 24 hours and follow any shorter ingredient use-by date. Reheat the potato once until steaming hot throughout, then add the cold toppings immediately before eating.

title: Shift Club Turkey Loaded Wrap
method: Make the filling first. Warm the cooked turkey breast through in the hot pan until piping hot and lightly coloured. It is already cooked, so stop before it dries out.

Keep the lettuce, tomato and other fresh/crunchy ingredients out of the pan. Mix the measured sauce or dressing with the cooked turkey breast; if the filling is being served hot, reduce only the sauce-coated cooked turkey breast until it is no longer wet enough to soak the wrap.
